title: Tokenizer JIT kernels + co-scheduling to cut prompt preprocess tail-latency
creator: Maya Patel
description: Investigate and implement a combined approach of JIT-compiling hot tokenizer paths and co-scheduling tokenizer worker threads with decode workers to reduce prefill-side CPU tail latency for short-to-medium prompts. Focus areas: (1) identify hot byte sequences and compile microkernels for BPE/wordpiece loops, (2) enforce core affinity so tokenizer and decoder tasks avoid contention on shared cores, (3) introduce fast early-exit for <32-token prompts and a lightweight session-level tokenization snapshot cache to avoid repeated work across retries/calls.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end median prefill CPU time reduced by >=30% on our 8-vCPU benchmark for typical customer prompts
p99 prefill CPU tail latency reduced by >=50% for short prompts (<64 tokens)
No regression in tokenizer correctness (all roundtrip tests pass) and no change to token IDs
Feature gated and can be rolled back via runtime-1.22 feature flag in Console
comments: 2026-03-01 - Maya Patel: Created ticket after profiling spike on collector-prod where prefill CPU was dominating p99 on small requests. Initial hypothesis: tokenizer hot loops and core contention with decoder workers.

2026-03-03 - Diego Alvarez: Completed flamegraph analysis on 8-vCPU instance. Findings: 68% of cycles in tokenization occur in byte->codepoint conversion and BPE lookup. Syscall and memcopy overhead small. Attached flamegraphs.

2026-03-05 - Diego Alvarez: Prototype JIT with LLVM ORC for the ASCII fastpath. Microbench: median tokenization time 12ms -> 7.8ms (35% median improvement), p99 210ms -> 110ms. Issues: binary size + cold-start JIT cost (~15ms) for first compilation.

2026-03-06 - Priya Singh (review): Reviewed prototype. Concern: JIT increases startup jitter for low-traffic Lambdas. Suggest fallbacks: precompiled microkernels packaged for common platforms and a runtime feature flag to disable JIT in Private deployments.

2026-03-07 - Diego Alvarez: Implemented core-affinity scheduler patch that pins tokenizer threads to dedicated cores and decoder to separate cores. Local testing: p99 further reduced to ~60ms under synthetic 2x concurrency workload. Added heuristics to avoid stealing cores when autoscaling triggers.

2026-03-08 - QA (E. Moore): Ran integration tests across models with different tokenization schemes (BPE, SentencePiece). Found edge case where NFKC normalization order affected token boundaries for multi-byte Unicode sequences. Patch applied to preserve canonical ordering in JIT kernels.

2026-03-09 - Diego Alvarez: Added session-level tokenization snapshot cache (per-connection canonicalized input -> token sequence) and early-exit when input length < 32 tokens. Combined effect reduces median by ~40% and p99 by ~65% on our real request traces. Pushed draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821

2026-03-10 - Maya Patel: Plan for rollout: feature flag enabled for hosted-dev first, collect telemetry for two weeks, then enable for staged Dedicated pools with toggle in Console. Coordinate with SDK team to add diagnostics for tokenization-mode (jit|precompiled|fallback).

Open items: provide precompiled microkernel artifacts for linux-x86_64 and amd64-arm64; add metrics for JIT compile time vs tokenization time; update runbooks if cache eviction causes correctness issues.
